messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=edge-lb-prod (P1) — health check failure rate > 50% across us-east-1 pool-A. auto-page sent to on-call.
Ryan (oncall): @pagerduty-bot acked — i'm pulling logs and will triage. :mag:
Maya (SRE): seeing TLS handshake errors (TLSError: illegal_parameter) from health-checkers -> targets flapping unhealthy. raw counts: 1200 req/min, 30% failed; backend 10/16 targets unhealthy in pool-A.
Jordan (NetOps): ran dig from multiple vantage points — authoritative still returning both edge1/edge2 A records but external resolver cache shows old edge2 IP in some regions.
Jordan (NetOps): dig +short @8.8.8.8 edge.prod.redwood.com -> 54.210.33.120
Jordan (NetOps): dig +short @1.1.1.1 edge.prod.redwood.com -> 3.120.45.9
Maya (SRE): health-check logs show client SNI=hc.internal.redwood.local while cert SAN only includes edge.prod.redwood.com — health checks are failing TLS due to SNI mismatch after we switched the health-check hostname in last week's rollout.
Omar (Eng Lead): agree this looks like health-check SNI regression. Proposed quick mitigation: switch pool-A health-check to TCP mode (no TLS) and shift traffic to pool-B, then roll certs/healthcheck hostname fix behind a canary.
Maya (SRE): quick command to set tcp healthcheck (runbook):
```
redwoodctl infra healthcheck update --pool pool-A --type tcp --port 8080
redwoodctl route weight set --route edge.prod --from pool-A:100 --to pool-B:0 --step 25 --interval 60s
```
Ryan (oncall): executing tcp healthcheck flip now.
incident-bot: action log — runbook step executed by Ryan at 1777554360.
Maya (SRE): switching to TCP removed TLS handshake failures immediately, targets recovered to 95% healthy within 90s.
Jordan (NetOps): starting controlled weight shift to pool-B as Omar suggested. monitoring DNS TTL propagation for edge2 updates — TTL is 300s.
Elaine (QA): confirming external client tests — curl from EU shows 200 OK to edge after shift, older clients still show handshake fails when routed to legacy IPs.
Omar (Eng Lead): customer impact: estimated 2.7% global request error rate during window; primarily API customers with strict TLS client stacks and some old resolvers. Not seeing persistent data loss.
Ryan (oncall): paging notes: acknowledged at 1777554330, mitigated at 1777554395. I'll open INC-2332 in ops and assign to Maya/Jordan for postmortem.
pagerduty-bot: Escalation check — service acknowledged, no further escalation.
Maya (SRE): postmortem action items: (1) revert health-check hostname change or add SAN for hc.internal, (2) add canary for health-check TLS verification, (3) update runbook commands.
Omar (Eng Lead): will create pull request for cert SAN and schedule canary deploy tomorrow morning.
Elaine (QA): logging note — add telemetry metric for health-check TLS mismatch to alert earlier.
Ryan (oncall): closing thread. :white_check_mark:
